_comment: Per-model parameter constraints for Human-in-the-Loop tool-call editing. Keyed by tool name, then by model. 'modelId' is the cfgpu-internal model id and stays the operational key (model_tool_configs.model_id); 'modelName' is the cfgpu MCP's public model identifier — the value the MCP's 'model' tool parameter now accepts (its enum lists model_name only; adapterId / cfgpu_model_id are never exposed). The two differ for the dated/renamed models (e.g. modelId doubao-seedance-2-0-260128 -> modelName doubao-seedance-2-0, nano-pro -> cf-pro), so a caller building a generate_* tool call must send modelName, not modelId. The per-entry args.model options/value carry modelName values accordingly — that field is what actually goes on the wire, so it must match the MCP enum, whereas modelId is only a DB key. 'args' maps the unified (generic) arg names from tool_registry.py to the REAL value range/type of the underlying model (extracted from each model's card.md/adapter.yaml). Params a model does NOT support are omitted from that model's entry. quality_tier drives model='auto' routing, so it is listed on the 'auto' entry; it ALSO appears on the per-model entries whose adapter maps it into the payload (kling-video-o1 / kling-v3-omni -> mode, gpt-image-2 -> quality), where it stays meaningful after the model is fixed. Models whose entry omits it ignore it once selected. writable=false means the field is fixed/control-only and should not be exposed for editing. An enum's 'options' carries two shapes: usually a list of bare wire values, but where the wire value is not what a human should be shown it is a list of {label, value} objects instead (currently quality_tier, whose fast/balanced/best read as speed rather than the 低/中/高 quality they actually select). A consumer must handle both; 'value' is always what goes on the wire, and 'default' is always a wire value, never a label. model_specific is a free-form passthrough dict (passthrough=true): its 'fields' map lists the documented per-model sub-keys with their ranges; users may still pass additional undocumented keys.

aspect_ratio.note: mapped to an exact pixel pair (width*height — a star, not seedream's x) computed inside the tier's total-pixel budget, so the emitted ratio is exact. Because pixels go up rather than a tier name, aspect_ratio governs even when reference_images are present; with a tier name upstream would instead scale the output to the LAST input image's ratio. To hand framing back to the model, set model_specific.parameters.size to 1K or 2K

resolution.note: tier names are total-pixel budgets (1K = 1024x1024, 2K = 2048x2048) inside an all-scenario range of [768x768, 2048x2048]; 4K exists only on wan2.7-image-pro. 1.5K / 3K / 4K are rejected before the request is sent, not silently downgraded — validate_only reports the nearest tier at or below in corrected_args, and model=auto routes such a request elsewhere

reference_images.note: 0-9 images; array order is the 图N ordinal the prompt and bbox_list refer to. JPEG / JPG / PNG (no alpha) / BMP / WEBP, each side 240-8000 px, ratio within [1:8, 8:1], <= 20 MB

regions.note: user-drawn regions [{image_index, box:[x1,y1,x2,y2] normalised to [0,1], label?, note?, image_size?}]. Not hand-editable: a box comes from what the user marked on the canvas, and a typed-in coordinate is exactly the transcription this parameter exists to avoid. On this model they map to parameters.bbox_list in ABSOLUTE pixels of the original image, so every region MUST carry image_size ([width, height] of the original, not of the display canvas) — a request without it is refused, never guessed, because a wrong size does not fail, it edits a plausible billed rectangle elsewhere. maxItems is per image (2), and regions cannot be combined with n>1

image_refs.note: one caller handle per image, same order and length as reference_images; resolves [[handle]] placeholders in prompt so the caller never hard-codes an image ordinal. Never sent upstream. On this model a [[label]] placeholder resolves to neutral wording (e.g. 图2中框选的区域) rather than to coordinates, since the coordinates travel in parameters.bbox_list

n.note: CEILING on the image-set size (图像集), not an exact count: the model decides how many images the set holds and n only caps it, so fewer than n is a normal outcome and no upstream setting forces an exact number. n>1 sends enable_sequential=true together with n, never one without the other — enable_sequential alone defaults n to 12 upstream, i.e. a 12-image bill. At n=1 neither key is sent. Cannot be combined with regions

sample_rate.note: output sample rate in Hz (e.g. 24000, 32000); null = model default

bitrate.note: output bitrate in bps (MiniMax only, e.g. 128000); null = model default

emotion.note: emotion hint, e.g. happy/sad/angry (MiniMax only); null lets the model infer from text

quality_tier.note: router selection preference; no effect once a specific model is chosen

model_specific.note: documented sub-fields depend on the resolved model; see that model's entry

generate_audio.note: Synchronous text-to-speech, high-fidelity tier. Supports the full MiniMax voice-control set (speed/volume/pitch/emotion/bitrate). Billed per character.

text.note: text to synthesize (required); supports inline emotion/event tags like (laughs)

voice.note: maps to input.voice_setting.voice_id; 327 system voices across 中文/粤语/英/日/韩/西/葡/法 etc. — see card.md for the full list

model_specific.note: merged at the top of input; other direct MiniMax fields

text.note: text to synthesize (required); supports inline emotion/event tags like (laughs)

voice.note: maps to input.voice_setting.voice_id; 327 system voices — see minimax-speech-2-8-hd card.md for the full list

model_specific.note: merged at the top of input; other direct MiniMax fields

generate_audio.note: Asynchronous text-to-speech (submit then poll). 122 expressive Chinese system voices (角色扮演/有声阅读/客服/视频配音), emotion + ASMR support. Only voice / audio_format / sample_rate are used — speed/volume/pitch/emotion/bitrate are MiniMax-only and ignored here.

voice.note: maps to req_params.speaker; *_uranus_bigtts voices support 情感变化/指令遵循/ASMR — see card.md for the full list

model_specific.note: merged at the top of req_params; other direct seed-tts fields

understand_vision.note: Unified tool schema from UnderstandVisionInput. Vision-language: returns a TEXT answer (not media). Always synchronous — no task_id, no wait/timeout. prompt is required even when media is attached.

images.note: public image URLs; multiple images reasoned over jointly

video.note: a single public video URL (long video supported)

regions.note: user-drawn regions [{image_index, box:[x1,y1,x2,y2] normalised to [0,1], label?, note?, image_size?}]. Not hand-editable: a box comes from what the user marked on the canvas, and a typed-in coordinate is exactly the transcription this parameter exists to avoid. Only models with the region_understand capability accept it; passing it to another model is a hard error, never a silent whole-image answer

image_refs.note: one caller handle per image, same order and length as images; resolves [[handle]] placeholders in prompt so the caller never hard-codes an image ordinal. Never sent upstream

system_prompt.note: null = generic 'You are a helpful assistant.'

max_tokens.note: max output tokens; null = model default

return_metadata.note: include token usage; the answer is always returned (reasoning_content only on Thinking models, which the current catalog has none of)

model_specific.note: documented sub-fields depend on the resolved model; see that model's entry

understand_vision.note: Vision-language understanding/reasoning over images & video. Synchronous via OpenAI-compatible /model/v1/chat/completions; 128K context; cost 2/5, speed 4/5. Capabilities: image understanding/reasoning, video understanding (long video), long document, tool calling, visual agent, long context. Returns text, not media — no wait/timeout/watermark. Not a Thinking variant: no reasoning_content.

images.note: maps to messages[user].content[].image_url.url; multiple images reasoned over jointly

video.note: maps to messages[user].content[].video_url.url; single video, long video supported

regions.note: user-drawn regions [{image_index, box:[x1,y1,x2,y2] normalised to [0,1], label?, note?, image_size?}]. Not hand-editable: a box comes from what the user marked on the canvas, and a typed-in coordinate is exactly the transcription this parameter exists to avoid. Only models with the region_understand capability accept it; passing it to another model is a hard error, never a silent whole-image answer

image_refs.note: one caller handle per image, same order and length as images; resolves [[handle]] placeholders in prompt so the caller never hard-codes an image ordinal. Never sent upstream

system_prompt.note: maps to messages[system].content; null = 'You are a helpful assistant.'

max_tokens.note: maps to max_tokens; null = model default

temperature.note: maps to temperature; null = model default

return_metadata.note: include token usage; choices[0].message.content (the answer) is always returned

model_specific.note: merged at the top level of the chat/completions request
